items.title: nvidia's auto-ontology takes the top spot with 2,707 stars
items.summary:
nvidia's python framework builds a semantic layer over business data so agents can query tables without guessing what a column means.
it is at 6,728 stars and was pushed at 14:45 utc, up from 2,050 stars at this morning's build.

items.title: agent-desktop slips to second but still adds 2,173 stars
items.summary:
the rust cli lets agents drive desktop apps through accessibility trees instead of guessing from screenshots.
it is at 16,396 stars, about 1,000 more than this morning, and vercel last pushed it at 06:31 utc.

items.title: mattpocock's skills repo climbs to 2,053 stars today
items.summary:
it is a shell repo of agent skills copied straight from the author's .agents directory, with no framework attached.
it sits at 314,587 stars and is the third-fastest mover on the daily chart.

items.title: scrapling holds 1,661 stars as scraping demand persists
items.summary:
the python framework handles anything from one request to a full crawl, with anti-bot handling built in.
it is at 97,597 stars but has not been pushed since yesterday, unlike every repo above it.

items.title: discimage studio enters the chart with 977 stars
items.summary:
the c# tool inspects and rebuilds disc images, a niche utility that suddenly found a crowd.
it is at 7,096 stars and was pushed at 14:01 utc, so the repo is still active today.

items.title: floci keeps 784 stars for a local aws emulator
items.summary:
it runs aws services locally in java so agent tests do not need a cloud account.
it is at 30,139 stars and was pushed at 15:58 utc, so development has not slowed.

items.title: gstack arrives with 608 stars for a ready-made claude code setup
items.summary:
it packages 23 opinionated tools and prompts meant to run a small company's engineering workflow.
it is at 139,744 stars and was pushed at 15:58 utc, so the repo is still active today.

items.title: worktrunk holds 546 stars for parallel agent worktrees
items.summary:
the rust cli manages git worktrees so several coding agents can work in one repo without collisions.
it is at 11,371 stars, a small but steady gain from 531 at this morning's build.

items.title: arab parties back eisenkot for pm, handing him a majority
items.summary:
the joint list and ra'am told president herzog they want gadi eisenkot to form the next government, and the democrats did the same.
that puts him past the 61-seat threshold, but eisenkot wants coalition partners to call hamas a terrorist group and abbas has stopped short.
items.change: yesterday herzog had only opened consultations; today two arab-led parties and the democrats formally recommended eisenkot.

items.title: saudi air defenses intercept a houthi missile aimed at medina
items.summary:
the saudi-led coalition said it destroyed a ballistic missile fired toward the medina region and a drone over the eastern province.
riyadh also issued potential-danger alerts for yanbu, its main red sea oil export hub, and for sharurah on the yemen border.
items.change: the coalition reported only a drone over makkah on tuesday; today it reported a ballistic missile at medina, a drone over the eastern province and alerts for yanbu.

items.title: houthis reportedly ask saudi arabia for $51bn to stop fighting
items.summary:
the wall street journal reported the group wants $51bn in compensation and recognition as yemen's rulers in exchange for ending attacks.
saudi arabia approached the houthis after attacks on red sea tankers, and has not publicly accepted either demand.
items.change: the price for a ceasefire is now public: $51bn plus recognition, which would undercut the government riyadh backs.

items.title: three more vessels burn in hormuz as iran keeps up pressure
items.summary:
the irgc said two oil tankers and a tugboat caught fire after using what it called an unauthorized route through the strait.
uk maritime trade operations also logged a tanker hit by two projectiles 50 nautical miles north of qatar, with damage still unconfirmed.
items.change: iran is pressing the same tactic after the us vote, adding a third burning hull and a strike off qatar to yesterday's mine claims.

items.title: iran's security chief carries a khamenei message to putin
items.summary:
mohsen rezaei met vladimir putin in the kremlin and delivered a message from supreme leader mojtaba khamenei, iran's state broadcaster said.
the visit follows leaked documents showing russia agreed to supply 90 helicopter missile launchers, which the guardian says were ordered for iran.
items.change: tehran moved from phone diplomacy to a kremlin visit, and the russian arms pipeline is now documented rather than suspected.

items.title: vance blames the iran war for the republican rout
items.summary:
the vice president wrote that 'the reason we lost is the war', and iran's parliament speaker mocked him for 'losing-gambler energy'.
republican lawmakers are instead blaming pete hegseth, and the house could vote on impeachment as soon as next week.
items.change: yesterday trump accepted the result; today his own vice president named the war as the cause and the party turned on its defense secretary.

items.title: yemen's president sacks ministers as the front line moves closer
items.summary:
the presidential leadership council dismissed ministers and senior officers after its october counteroffensive failed to push the houthis back.
the who says 1,771 people have been killed in yemen since august, with 94 of them in the last week of october.
items.change: the government has gone from claiming advances in al-jawf to firing its own commanders, and the who put a number on the toll.

items.title: saudi and iranian foreign ministers talk regional security
items.summary:
prince faisal bin farhan took a call from abbas araghchi and both sides said they discussed efforts to strengthen regional security.
the call came hours after houthi missiles were aimed at saudi cities, and it is the clearest sign riyadh still keeps a direct line to tehran.
items.change: a direct minister-level call is new, and it landed on the same day houthi missiles were fired at saudi cities.

watch.title: Shipping crews caught in the crossfire of the Hormuz conflict
Republicans turn against Hegseth after election losses

items.title: nasdaq drops 5% into correction as tech leads a broad selloff
items.summary:
the nasdaq composite fell 5.0% to 24,448 and the s&p 500 lost 3.3% to 7,437 as investors kept rotating out of ai names.
the dow fell 1,230 points to 52,126 despite gains in chevron and johnson & johnson, and the vix jumped 56% to 25.94.

items.title: ai hardware and neoclouds lead a second day of selling
items.summary:
the semiconductor etf soxx fell 11.8%, with nvidia and broadcom down 8.9% and 9.2% and oracle down 8.7%.
neoclouds fell harder: coreweave -15.9%, nebius -19.0% and iren -20.7%, while tesla dropped 11.0%.
items.change: the morning build had this as a rotation out of data centres; today it widened into the biggest chip and neocloud names and dragged the index down.

items.title: qualcomm falls 14% on weak guidance and a memory crunch
items.summary:
the chipmaker beat on earnings but guided next quarter to $2.15-2.35 a share against $2.27 expected.
handset chip sales fell 26% to $5.14bn as memory costs pushed phone prices up, and the stock was last down 13.9%.

items.title: oil reverses and climbs back above $90
items.summary:
wti rose 2.2% to $90.04 and brent 2.3% to $96.83, one day after both fell more than 8%.
traders are weighing whether a democratic congress can actually end the war, and tanker attacks in hormuz are still disrupting cargoes.
items.change: yesterday's collapse was the story; today crude gave back part of it as the hormuz attacks continued.

items.title: barkin says the fed will probably have to hike again
items.summary:
the richmond fed president said unemployment is near record lows and inflation too high, so the path is 'pretty straightforward'.
markets price a better than 80% chance of a december hike, even as the 10-year yield fell to 4.83% on the tech selloff.

items.title: claims stay low and productivity jumps, while the boe hikes
items.summary:
initial jobless claims fell to 189,000 and third-quarter productivity rose 3.6% as unit labour costs fell 0.7%.
the bank of england raised rates to 4% in a 9-0 vote, its first increase in more than three years, and warned inflation will near 5%.
items.change: the us data came in stronger than forecast, and the boe delivered the hike the market expected but with a unanimous vote.

items.title: airbnb and cloudflare lead the after-the-bell slate
items.summary:
conocophillips and sony reported before the open, and airbnb, cloudflare, atlassian, eog and microchip report after the close.
with chips already selling off, microchip's guidance will matter more than its quarterly beat or miss.
items.change: this morning the focus was conocophillips and sony; tonight it shifts to airbnb, cloudflare and microchip.

items.title: gold rises as the dollar and yields slip
items.summary:
gold futures rose 1.0% to $4,112.50 and silver held near $52 as traders moved into defensive assets.
the 10-year treasury yield fell to 4.83% and the dollar weakened after the midterms, both of which help bullion.
items.change: gold added another 1% after yesterday's 1.8% gain, with the move now driven by the tech selloff rather than the election.

items.title: iraola says liverpool conceded 'cheap and messy' goals in istanbul
items.summary:
liverpool led twice through trey nyoni's first senior goal and an isak header, then lost 3-2 to fenerbahce.
iraola refused to blame rotation and defended starting barcola up front, while a bbc fan video picked out jacquet's errors.
items.change: the morning build had the scoreline; today it is iraola's explanation and the first detailed post-match criticism.

items.title: palace away on sunday with harrington in charge
items.summary:
liverpool go to selhurst park on sunday for a 2pm gmt kick-off, 5pm in riyadh.
tony harrington will referee, michael salisbury is on var, and iraola speaks to the press on friday.
items.change: the officials and kick-off time are now confirmed; at the morning build the fixture was only pencilled in.

items.title: nyoni's first senior goal strengthens his case for a new deal
items.summary:
the 19-year-old scored liverpool's opener in istanbul and said the team has to 'bounce back quickly'.
the echo says talks over a new deal are under way after a display that stood out on a bad night.
items.change: he had a strong game yesterday; today he has his first senior goal and has spoken about the response.

items.title: araujo's permanent move looks likelier at £47m
items.summary:
the echo says liverpool hold a £47m option on the barcelona centre-back and that his new agent has met the club.
barcelona are chasing another defender, which would make the loan permanent, while fussball news links liverpool to frankfurt's nnamdi collins.
items.change: yesterday the talk was chiesa's exit; today it is a concrete option price on araujo plus a new scouting link.

meta.reliability: araujo from the echo; collins from fussball news, low

items.title: gravenberch has a fractured heel and is out in istanbul
items.summary:
iraola said the midfielder has a heel fracture and was left at the axa centre, with sunday's trip to palace uncertain.
he felt it warming up against arsenal, and with palace on sunday the club chose not to risk the flight.

items.title: kuyt's interim spell produces a 'miracle' against his old club
items.summary:
dirk kuyt, the former liverpool winger, is fenerbahce's interim boss and said the comeback mentality came from liverpool.
he called it 'a miracle' and said not many expected fenerbahce to win after liverpool led twice.

items.title: bournemouth visit anfield in the carabao cup on 16 december
items.summary:
the quarter-final is set for wednesday 16 december at 20:00 gmt, shown on itv and sky in the uk.
it sits in a run of six games in 18 days, which is why rotation in istanbul matters more than usual.

items.title: wright's second youth hat-trick wins a 3-5 thriller
items.summary:
will wright scored three as liverpool's u19s beat fenerbahce 5-3 in the youth league in istanbul.
it was his second hat-trick in the competition and came in a game that also had a red card.
